sanskrit_verse:
अङ्गादङ्गात् संभवति पुत्रवद्दुहिता नृणाम् ।
तस्मात्पितृधनं त्वन्यः कथं गृह्णीत मानवः ॥
transliteration: aṅgād aṅgāt saṃbhavati putravad duhitā nṛṇām / tasmāt pitṛdhanaṃ tv anyaḥ kathaṃ gṛhṇīta mānavaḥ //
sph_interpretive_translation: From the body of a man arises the daughter, equal in essence to the son; therefore, how can another being claim ownership over the father's wealth?
jurisprudential_principles: Causation is rooted in embodied manifestation
Capacity-based responsibility derives from existential source
Restoration logic aligns inheritance with generative origin
Consciousness alignment demands recognition of filial equality
executable_legal_axioms: IF offspring arises from embodied origin THEN inheritance rights are equally distributed among all biological progeny
IF claimant lacks generative causality THEN property assertion is nullified without restitution process
IF gender-based distinction is applied THEN automatic realignment to ontological equity is enforced
IF proprietary conflict arises THEN resolution defaults to primacy of generative lineage
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating inheritance disputes, the Supreme Court shall recognize that ontological origin supersedes social convention. The principle of embodied causation establishes equal proprietary capacity for all children arising from the same source-body, regardless of gender or societal role.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that a daughter manifests directly from the father's body, identical in causal basis to a son. Therefore, exclusion from inheritance violates anupūrvaśaḥ — the sequential manifestation of dharma. Responsibility lies in restoring alignment through recognition, not punitive correction of error.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Immediate cessation of inequitable asset distribution
Public acknowledgment of filial equality before governing council
Reintegration ceremony affirming daughter's proprietary status
Legal document revision to reflect ontological inheritance truth
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of Law: inheritance belongs to those who arise from the source-body, without distinction. Dharma is restored through recognition of embodied causality. Reality is non-punitive; consciousness alone adjudicates truth.
